about: Where the judge may look when the rulings record, the scripts and the skill's own files don't answer a question. Anything not listed here is not a source. 'level' follows plan 028: 1 official, 2 binding for tournaments or one format, 4 judge and community consensus; null means a finding aid that is never cited.

sources.name: Scryfall API
sources.good_for: Oracle text, Wizards' rulings per card, legality
sources.cite_as: Use card.py; cite the card's Oracle text or the dated Wizards ruling

sources.name: Gatherer
sources.good_for: Wizards' own card database and rulings
sources.cite_as: The card name and the ruling's date

sources.name: Wizards of the Coast: rules, release notes, announcements
sources.good_for: The Comprehensive Rules; each set's release notes (the fullest official rulings for new cards); rules changes; banned and restricted lists
sources.cite_as: The page title, its date and its URL

sources.name: Wizards Play Network: rules documents
sources.good_for: The Magic Tournament Rules, the Infraction Procedure Guide, Judging at Regular REL
sources.cite_as: Use sources.py and lookup.py --doc; cite the section and the version

sources.name: Format sites
sources.good_for: Oathbreaker's own rules and banned list (Commander's are on magic.wizards.com)
sources.cite_as: The page and its own rule numbers, which are not CR numbers

sources.name: Magic Judges Rules Resources
sources.good_for: The rules documents with a link per rule; the annotated MTR and IPG; the Missed Triggers Guides
sources.cite_as: The article, its author and date; for the documents themselves cite the official version

sources.name: Cranial Insertion
sources.good_for: Judge-written answers about specific interactions. The newest found was from June 2025; older ones may predate rules changes
sources.cite_as: The article, its author and date

sources.name: Judge Foundry
sources.good_for: Judge training material from the judge organisation for the US and Canada
sources.cite_as: The page, its author and date

sources.name: Academy Ruins
sources.good_for: Older versions of the CR, MTR and IPG, and what changed between them
sources.cite_as: Never: cite the official document it mirrors

sources.name: Yawgatog
sources.good_for: The CR with a link per rule
sources.cite_as: Never: cite the official document it mirrors

sources.name: MTG Wiki
sources.good_for: Finding out which rules and terms are involved

excluded.what: Reddit, Stack Exchange and other forums
excluded.why: Decided 2026-10-25: not read, not stored, not cited, even when a user pastes a post in

excluded.what: AI-written answers and summaries, search-engine overviews included, and the judge's own earlier answers
excluded.why: They are not sources; check what they claim against the documents instead

excluded.what: Copies of the CR or other documents on sites not listed here, and anything with no author or date
excluded.why: Their version and accuracy can't be checked

people.what: Judge chat: chat.magicjudges.org, or #magicjudges-rules on Libera.Chat
people.use: Suggest it to the user when the skill can't settle a question. A judge's answer the user brings back goes into the ruling's deliberation, with who said it and when

rules: Check every web page's date against the current CR's effective date. An answer written before a rules change doesn't count.
A ruling backed only by level 4 sources is at most 'likely', and the answer says so.
A web page a ruling cites goes in the citation with its URL, title, date and an excerpt.
